info.name: STRIKE API
info.description:
API collection for STRIKE, the cross-border pricing/quoting engine. Import the accompanying "STRIKE - Local" environment alongside this collection and select it before sending requests.

There is no public registration endpoint — accounts are created by an admin (eventually via the admin dashboard; for now, run `node ace create:user` in apps/server to create a login for testing this collection).

request.description:
Logs in an existing user with email + password. Returns the user's public info and a new bearer token valid for 30 days.

Fails with 400 for an unknown email or an incorrect password (same error either way, so it can't be used to discover registered emails).

Returns the currently authenticated user, identified by the bearer token saved from Login.

Fails with 401 if the token is missing, invalid, or has been logged out.
Read-only lookup data seeded from the old project's reference tables. Similar endpoints exist for /reference/regions, /currencies, /use-cases, /integration-types, and /icp-nodes.
The master corridor catalog a user picks from when adding a corridor to a quote. Supports optional ?countryId=&serviceCode=&transactionTypeCode= filters.

query.description: true to exclude any payer containing "swift wire transfer" from every count
true to restrict the whole picker to the old app's compliance country allow-list (mirrors selecting "Last Mile Payout"/"Account Top-Up" as a use case)

request.description: Powers the "Corridors to Offer" picker: per-dimension counts (regions, countries, services, transaction types, payout currencies, payers) plus totalAvailable/totalMatched, given any combination of the query filters. Every dimension supports multiple selected values (OR within a dimension, AND across dimensions). Prefer repeated, URL-encoded bracket-array parameters, for example countryIds[]=44&countryIds[]=47. Legacy comma-separated lists remain supported. For payer names containing commas or ampersands, use payerCodes[]=Bank%2C%20Branch%20%26%20Partners so punctuation remains part of one value. Both this endpoint and GET /reference/corridors/matching use the same parser and reject malformed filters with 422. Empty parameters clear a filter. The matching endpoint returns { corridors: [...] }, capped at 200 rows; this endpoint supplies the uncapped totalMatched. Region is a one-way filter: it narrows every other dimension but is never itself narrowed, even by its own filter — the other five dimensions narrow each other mutually (never by their own filter). Every panel always lists every value that exists, even ones with count 0, so the UI can disable rather than remove them.

Creates a new quote, owned by the current user, always starting in 'draft' status.

Most fields are optional besides name — this example shows the multi-value ones (a quote can have several funding/source currencies and use cases, matching the old app exactly). Other optional fields: partnerCountryId, integrationTypeId, icpLevel1Id/icpLevel2Id/icpLevel3Id, contractLengthYears, waivedMonths, partnerPrCode, showFxSourceInContract, showFxSpreadInContract, fxModel, selectedPricingStrategy, selectedFxPricing, defaultFeeCurrencyId. Currency/use-case ids depend on what's seeded — check "List Countries"/"Currencies" first if these don't exist in your database.

The corridorFilter* fields are the "Corridors to Offer" facet-filter selection (Region/Country/Service/Transaction Type/Payout Currency/Payer, plus a Hide USD SWIFT flag) — they drive the Pricing tab's live preview rows and default to empty arrays / false when omitted.
Lists the current user's own quotes (an admin sees every quote).
Returns the full quote (with its corridors) plus backend-computed totals (revenue, margin, take rate) — the client never computes these itself.
Only allowed while the quote is still in 'draft' status — fails with 409 once submitted.

Adds a corridor from the catalog to the quote. The backend computes revenue/FX margin/margin fee/gross margin/take-rate using the corridor's real cost/FX-source master data, and flags approval via two independent checks: needs_financial_approval (margin/pricing rules, with financial_approval_reasons) and needs_network_approval (a lookup on the corridor catalog's own Need Approval/Internal/Central Bank fields, with network_approval_reasons) — needs_approval/approval_reasons remain the combined OR of both for backward compatibility. None of this is trusted from the request body. Run "List Corridors (catalog)" first to populate {{corridor_id}}. Optionally accepts a `fundingCurrencyId` — the same corridor can be added once per funding currency on the quote (Phase B); repeating this request unchanged (same corridor, same funding currency or none) returns 409. See "Add Corridor to Quote (Different Funding Currency)".

item.name: Add Corridor to Quote (Different Funding Currency)

request.description: Phase B: the same corridor, added again under a different `{{funding_currency_id}}` than any already used for it on this quote — succeeds (201) as an independent row, rather than the 409 you'd get from repeating "Add Corridor to Quote" unchanged. Run "List Currencies" first to populate {{funding_currency_id}}.

Splits a corridor's yearly volume across up to 3 tiers (each with its own fixed fee/variable fee %/FX spread), with whatever volume isn't assigned to a tier pricing at the corridor's own standard fields above. Tier 1 = smallest discount, Tier 3 = biggest. Tier volumes can never sum to more than yearlyVolumeUsd — a 422 is returned otherwise. Response includes a `tiers` array with each tier's own computed revenue/margin/approval, plus the corridor's top-level fields (revenueFee, totalRevenue, needsApproval, etc.) as the combined total across the standard remainder and every tier. Each tier's transaction count is derived from its volume ÷ atvUsd, not entered directly.

Updates pricing inputs for a corridor already on the quote — the backend recomputes revenue/FX margin/margin fee/gross margin/take-rate and both approval checks (financial + network, see "Add Corridor to Quote") from the merged values. Can also include `pricingModel` ("standard"/"tiered") and `tiers` (see "Add Tiered Corridor to Quote") — switching to "standard" deletes the corridor's tier rows; omitting `tiers` while already tiered re-prices using whatever tiers are already saved (e.g. after changing yearlyVolumeUsd alone). `fundingCurrencyId` is deliberately not accepted here (Phase B decision) — a row's funding currency is fixed once it exists; sending it is silently ignored rather than erroring.

Soft-deletes every id in `corridorIds` that's currently active on this quote. Returns `{ deletedIds, notFoundIds }` — ids that belong to a different quote, don't exist, or are already deleted land in `notFoundIds` instead of failing the whole request (idempotent partial success, not an error).
Lists this quote's currently soft-deleted corridors, with the same corridor/country/currency detail as "Show Quote" — the data source for a Restore picker UI.

request.description: Restores every id in `corridorIds` that's currently soft-deleted on this quote (its tiers come back exactly as they were). Returns `{ restoredIds, notFoundIds }` — ids that aren't currently deleted land in `notFoundIds`, not an error.

Soft-deletes the corridor (sets `deleted_at`) rather than removing the row — it disappears from the quote and its totals but can be brought back with "Bulk Restore Corridors". Placed after the bulk requests in this collection so it runs against the corridor while it's still active.

Returns `{ setupFee: null }` until the tab has been saved once, otherwise `{ setupFee: {...} }` with every backend-computed value (finalCommitmentFee, year1CommittedRevenue, totalContractValue, needsApproval, approvalReasons) plus its milestones/principal-slots/block-fees/other-fees.

request.description: Creates or replaces the quote's whole Setup Fee tab in one call (only allowed while the quote is in 'draft' status). The backend validates cross-field consistency (custom payment milestones must sum to exactly 100%, principal-based MCF must have enough slots for the contract length, waived months capped at 6 — the old app's own UI never actually allowed past 6 despite its input saying 24) and computes finalCommitmentFee/year1CommittedRevenue/totalContractValue/needsApproval/approvalReasons itself — none of that is trusted from the request body. otherFees concept codes: reversal_request, proof_of_payment, emergency_funding, treasury_management, business_hub_platform, post_funding_penalty, corridor_no_usage, white_glove, stablecoin_prefunding, digital_asset_icp_setup, bulk_currency_conversion, currencies_for_treasury. For a custom payment schedule, add a paymentMilestones array (milestones are only stored when paymentSchedule is 'custom'; a 'full' schedule clears any previously saved ones); for a principal-based MCF, add mcfPrincipalSlots (2 slots for a 12-month contract, 3 for longer).

Returns the quote's 3-year P&L projection, computed from saved (non-deleted, positive-volume) corridors and the saved Setup Fee — never unsaved preview edits. Response: { inputs: { year2GrowthPct, year3GrowthPct }, years: { year1, year2, year3 }, completeness: { corridorCount, hasSetupFee }, needsApproval, approvalReasons }. Growth defaults to 0/0 until PUT is called at least once; an explicitly saved 0% growth is never replaced with a guessed default.

Sets the two P&L growth inputs (Year2-over-1 %, Year3-over-2 %) — only allowed while the quote is in 'draft' status. Returns the same shape as GET, recomputed with the new inputs. Growth is bounded to [-100, 500]. Year 1 is never affected by growth; Year 2/3 corridor-derived figures compound from Year 1, while one-off Setup/Network fees apply to Year 1 only and MCF commitment-fee revenue for Year 2/3 comes from the real month-by-month MCF schedule, not a guess.

Read-only rollup for the Quoting Summary tab: partner info, contract details, the Setup Fee section, the P&L service's own financialProjections (byte-identical to a direct GET /pnl call — composed internally, never recomputed separately), and a corridor-by-region breakdown (unweighted average fee/spread using each corridor's actual quoted fixedFeeUsd/appliedFxSpread, never a catalog/minimum fallback). Missing partner region/country render as null plus a true flag in completeness, never a fake default. Uses the same saved/non-deleted/positive-volume corridor membership rule as P&L. corridorProjections is the corridor-only Year 1-3 view (volume, transactions, revenue = fee revenue + FX margin, no setup/commitment fees) derived from the same P&L years, so Year 1 revenue equals corridorsByRegionTotals.projectedRevenueUsd. setupFee.paymentMilestones is only populated when paymentSchedule is 'custom', ordered by sortOrder.

Read-only Final Quotation for the Legal tab, built from saved data only: one-off fee, fee/funding/source currencies, other pricing line items (zero items dropped), corridor rows (saved, non-deleted, volume > 0, sorted by country; fixed fee converted into the fee currency; FX spread/source only when the quote's show-in-contract flags are on; one row per tier for tiered corridors), commitment terms and payment terms. blockers lists everything the contract cannot invent (contract length, fee/funding/source currency, FX model, pricing strategy, Setup Fee, priced corridors, missing USD->fee-currency rate) — a missing rate is never treated as 1:1.

exec: pm.test('Returns an xlsx attachment, or 422 with blockers while the quote is incomplete', function () {

request.description: Downloads the Legal Contract workbook (sheet 'Quotation', title 'Legal Summary') generated on the server from the same data as Get Legal Data. Use Send and Download in Postman to save the file. Any quote status is allowed; until the quote is approved the sheet carries a 'DRAFT — this quote has not been approved' row. Returns 422 with { message, blockers } while Get Legal Data still lists blockers. Filename: 'Legal Contract - <PR code> - <quote name>.xlsx'.

The latest saved Fee Annex for the quote: { annex: { version, name, content, modifiedByName, createdAt, isStale } | null, suggestedName, hasSetupFee }. suggestedName is <Partner>_<PR>_<YYYYMMDD>_Fee_Annex (the old app's default). isStale is true when filling the saved document from the quote's current data would change it (a price, fee type, commitment or contract length changed since it was saved) — use Fill Fee Annex to refresh. Available at any quote status to the owner or an admin.
Metadata for every saved version, newest first (no content, and the editor's name rather than their email).

exec: pm.test('Saved (200) or rejected with a field error (422)', function () {

request.description: Saves the document as the next numbered version. Content is sanitized (script, event handlers, remote images and unsafe styles are removed) and the name is stored as plain text. Saving identical content and name is not a new version (changed: false). Allowed at any quote status, unlike other quote edits, so an approved quote's annex can still be corrected. Returns 422 { errors: [{ field, message }] } for an empty name or an annex with no content. Save Fee Annex does not fill values in — call Fill Fee Annex or Import Fee Annex first.

Returns the document filled from the quote's saved data without saving it: { content, warnings }. Fees, waiver, commitment periods, the selected one-off fee, the corridor table (only saved, non-deleted, volume > 0 corridors; FX columns follow the quote's show-in-contract flags) and the locked sections. Values sit in field markers and hidden rows are kept (display:none), so filling again after any change refreshes everything and can bring hidden rows back. A missing Setup Fee or contract length leaves the template text alone and adds a warning.

formdata.description: A .docx or .html annex template (up to 15 MB). PDFs are refused.

request.description: Converts an uploaded .docx (mammoth) or .html template, sanitizes it and fills it from the quote data. Returns { content, warnings, fileName } and saves nothing — review it, then Save Fee Annex. 422 { errors: [{ field: 'file', message }] } for a missing/unsupported/unreadable/empty file. Choose a file in the Body tab before sending.

exec: pm.test('PDF attachment, 404 without a saved annex, or 503 when Chrome is not configured', function () {

request.description: Renders the latest saved version to an A4 PDF with headless Chromium (needs CHROME_PATH on the server; otherwise 503). JavaScript is off and all network requests are blocked while rendering. Hidden rows are left out; until the quote is approved the first line reads 'DRAFT — quote not approved'. 404 { message: 'Save a Fee Annex first.' } when nothing is saved. Filename: Fee_Annex_<QuoteName>_STRIKE_<id>.pdf. Use Send and Download.

exec: pm.test('DOCX attachment or 404 without a saved annex', function () {

request.description: Builds a Word document from the latest saved version (server-side, from the same sanitized HTML as the PDF): headings, inline bold/italic/underline, line breaks, nested and numbered lists, tables with merged cells and real column widths, and inline images. Hidden rows are left out; marked DRAFT until the quote is approved. Filename: Fee_Annex_<QuoteName>_STRIKE_<id>.docx. Use Send and Download.
Only allowed while the quote is still in 'draft' status.

Revokes the current bearer token. Deliberately placed last in the collection — every other request needs the token, so logging out too early breaks everything after it. Run this manually whenever you're done, don't rely on "Run collection" order alone unless this folder truly runs last.
